sections.label: MSF social residential homes oversight
sections.summary: MSF oversees more than 60 social residential homes providing 24/7 care to almost 4,000 residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Today, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) oversees more than 60 social residential homes that provide 24/7 residential care to almost 4,000 residents.

sections.label: Bill uplifts social residential home care
sections.summary: The Bill uplifts care quality and consolidates licensing regimes, bringing 61 Homes with about 4,000 residents under it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: It is therefore important that we continually strive for higher quality care in social residential homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This Bill will uplift the quality of care across the social residential home sector and strengthen safeguards for the safety and well-being of residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, we will consolidate the existing licensing regimes for Sheltered Homes, and Homes for Children and Young Persons, which comprises Children’s Homes and Children Disability Homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In total, 61 Homes with about 4,000 residents will come under this Bill – a significant increase from the 35 Homes, with approximately 1,100 residents, that are currently licensed.

sections.label: Codes of Practice clarify care standards
sections.summary: Codes of Practice will give operators and residents greater clarity on expected standards of care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Moving forward, these Codes of Practice will provide greater clarity to both operators and residents on the standards of care that are expected from operators.

sections.label: Reasonable force and mechanical restraints prohibited
sections.summary: The use of reasonable force or mechanical restraints is prohibited unless under specified circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Second, the use of reasonable force or mechanical restraints is prohibited unless under specified circumstances.

sections.label: Board of Visitors independent checks
sections.summary: MSF will appoint a Board of Visitors to conduct independent checks on social residential homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, MSF will appoint a Board of Visitors to conduct independent checks on social residential homes.

sections.label: Comprehensive enforcement framework for errant operators
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a comprehensive enforcement framework as a deterrent against errant operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Our residents are highly vulnerable and we need effective levers to prevent and manage incidents, should they occur.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Therefore, under this Bill, we have introduced a comprehensive enforcement framework as a deterrent against errant operators.

sections.label: Unlicensed Home operating fine
sections.summary: The Bill makes operating an unlicensed Home punishable by a fine of up to $100,000, with the maximum jail term unchanged.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, the offence of operating a Home without a licence may now warrant a fine of no more than $100,000, with no change to the maximum jail term.

sections.label: MSF step-in orders
sections.summary: MSF can issue step-in orders to temporarily take over a failing operator's Home to ensure continuity of care for residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: MSF will also be able to issue step-in orders to temporarily take over a failing operator’s Home for continuity of care for residents.

sections.label: Homes covered by Bill
sections.summary: The Bill covers Adult Disability Homes, Homes for Children and Young Persons, Sheltered Homes and Welfare Homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Homes that fall under the scope of the Social Residential Homes Bill are Adult Disability Homes, which includes Adult Disability Hostels, Homes for Children and Young Persons which comprises Children’s Homes and Children Disability Homes, Sheltered Homes and Welfare Homes.

sections.label: Transition Support Package funding
sections.summary: MSF and NCSS set aside a $33 million Transition Support Package for social residential homes licensed under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To support operators in transitioning to a new licensing regime, MSF and the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) have set aside a $33 million Transition Support Package for all social residential homes that will be licensed under this Bill.

sections.label: Home staff harassment protection
sections.summary: Staff in these Homes are public service workers under the Protection from Harassment Act 2014 and receive enhanced protection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Staff in these Homes are “public service workers” under the Protection from Harassment Act 2014 and as such, will receive enhanced protection under that Act.

sections.label: Social service staff support
sections.summary: The passage states continued investment in staff growth and well-being, salary guideline reviews, progression pathways and upskilling support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We value your hard work and contributions and will continue to invest in your growth and well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We regularly review the NCSS Skills and Salary Guidelines and work with Social Service Agencies to ensure that salaries in the sector are competitive with comparable roles in competing markets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We have charted progression pathways through the Skills Framework for Social Service and will continue to provide support for staff to be equipped with the necessary competencies to upskill themselves and effectively deliver care.

sections.label: Support for social service employees
sections.summary: Social service employees can access NCSS well-being support resources, and the Bill reflects the Government's commitment to support the vulnerable with community partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: While we work to equip and empower leaders in social service agencies to create a supportive work environment, social service employees can also access well-being support resources provided by NCSS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This Bill reflects the Government’s commitment to uplift and strengthen support for the most vulnerable amongst us, in partnership with our community partners.

sections.label: Singapore ageing by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, Singapore will have one in four residents above the age of 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: By 2030, Singapore will have one in four residents above the age of 65.

sections.label: Penalty for unauthorised home operation
sections.summary: The penalty for unauthorised operation of a home is proposed to increase to a maximum fine of $100,000 and/or up to two years of imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The penalty for unauthorised operation of a home is proposed to increase from the current maximum fine of $5,000 and/or up to two years of imprisonment; to a maximum fine of $100,000 and/or up to two years of imprisonment.

sections.label: Transition Support Package sufficiency
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the one-off Transition Support Package is sufficient for homes with lesser resources and whether MSF can consider stepped-down support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Will the one-off Transition Support Package that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned in his opening speech be sufficient in helping the homes transit to the new licensing regime, especially for homes with much lesser resources?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can MSF consider a stepped-down support package to help defray the expected increases in recurring operational costs for a few more additional years?

sections.label: Staff retention, funding, technology for homes
sections.summary: Initiatives, diversified funding, private sector collaboration and technology can help homes, and MSF will support 61 social residential homes to be licensed under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Initiatives, such as mental health support for caregivers and career development opportunities, can contribute to staff satisfaction and retention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We should also explore diversified funding models that go beyond Government dependence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Increased collaboration with the private sector and philanthropic organisations can help create a more sustainable financial ecosystem for these homes and I hope the Government can play a useful matchmaker role in this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The homes should also be encouraged to leverage technology to improve care delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: From telemedicine to digital health monitoring, innovative solutions can enhance the quality of care and keep residents connected with their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We are told that MSF oversees a range of social residential homes that provide short- to long-term residential care to different residential profiles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We are told that MSF has taken feedback from Children's Homes, Children's Disability Homes, Sheltered Homes, Welfare Homes, Adult Disability Homes and Adult Disability Hostels, and MSF will support 61 social residential homes to be licensed under this Bill, once passed, to meet the requirements of the Bill.

sections.label: Consultative approach and transition flexibility
sections.summary: The Member hopes MSF will consult social service agencies and exercise flexibility, noting MSF will provide a one-off transition support package and pre-licensing checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I hope MSF will adopt a consultative approach with social service agencies before imposing requirements that, if not appropriately funded, may be difficult to meet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We are also told that MSF will support all social residential homes licensed under this Bill with a one-off transition support package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For social residential homes seeking to be licensed for the first time, MSF will also offer pre-licensing checks to identify areas for improvement prior to implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Granted that the 61 social residential homes may consist of organisations of different sizes, resources or strengths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I also hope that the Ministry will exercise sufficient flexibility so that all social residential homes have sufficient time and resources to make the necessary conversion to adapt to the new regulatory regime without being penalised, especially social residential homes who may have been relatively constrained by their resources.

sections.label: Social Residential Homes Bill
sections.summary: MSF says 61 social residential homes provide 24-hour care, and this Bill codifies rules for residents' welfare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: According to MSF, there are currently 61 such Homes run by various social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: They range from Children's Homes, Homes for the Disabled, Aged Homes, Welfare Homes for Women and six Homes, such as Angsana, Banyan, Meranti Home in Pelangi Village in my Jalan Kayu constituency for the destitute, some of whom suffer from mental illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: These Homes provide their residents with 24-hour by seven days residential accommodation and care as their own families or homes can no longer house them for a variety of reasons, often complex and not easy to resolve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: This Social Residential Homes Bill which codifies the rules and changes that are important for the protection of how the Homes should be run for the welfare and well-being of these vulnerable residents, our fellow Singaporeans, is thus much needed.

sections.label: New licensing regime penalties
sections.summary: MSF introduced a new licensing regime with criminal penalties and regulatory actions proportionate to comparable offences under other Acts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: Further, MSF has introduced a new licensing regime with criminal penalties and regulatory actions revised to be proportionate to comparable offences under other Acts, such as the Healthcare Services Act.

sections.label: Screening foreign staff background checks
sections.summary: The Member asks how MSF helps agencies verify foreign staff background checks, especially from countries with less developed records systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: On the screening of foreign staff, I will like to ask how is MSF helping the agencies to ensure if the background checks of these staff are true and correct, especially if they come from countries that may have less developed systems of records on criminal or civil acts of delinquency, abuse or violence.

sections.label: Board of Visitors and budgets
sections.summary: The Member urges MSF to expand the Board of Visitors and asks Government to fund purpose-built homes, citing MOE's SPED schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: The Board of Visitors forms an essential protective channel to give voices to some of these voiceless residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: I urge MSF to step up in expanding the group of the Board of Visitors for these Homes and encourage Singaporeans who have the compassion and commitment to step up and volunteer in these important roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: My final appeal is to the Government, including the Ministry of Finance, to consider providing more budgets for MSF to gradually convert these social residential homes for the vulnerable to purpose-built Homes, like what the Ministry of Education (MOE) did for special education (SPED) schools over the past decades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: MOE's efforts with the SPED schools have transformed what used to be disused and barely retrofitted SPED schools that I visited in the early 2000s, when I first entered the social service sector, to state-of-the-art well designed SPED Schools, like Pathlight School, that we see today in the Ang Mo Kio Group Representation Constituency where I serve as a Member of Parliament.

sections.label: Ageing and residential care licensing
sections.summary: By 2030 one in four Singaporeans will be over 65, so more affordable residential care is needed; the Bill introduces a licensing framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be over the age of 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That means more people will need affordable, accessible residential care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill introduces a licensing framework, which is good.

sections.label: Director-General capacity limits
sections.summary: The Bill gives the Director-General power to set capacity limits for social residential homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill also gives the Director-General the power to set capacity limits for social residential homes.

sections.label: Homes respect, care, staffing ratios
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Director-General set licensing conditions but does not require minimum staffing ratios in Homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is about having a home where residents are treated with respect, compassion and real care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill gives the Director-General the power to set licensing conditions, but nowhere does it say that the Homes must have minimum staffing ratios.

sections.label: Roadmap and minimum staffing ratios
sections.summary: It calls for a 10 to 20 year roadmap and minimum staffing ratios so every resident gets attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A set of rules is not the same as a system that truly cares.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need a roadmap, not just for today, but for the next 10 to 20 years, so that every Singaporean in need has a place to turn to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, quality care must be more than just words on a page.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need minimum staffing ratios so that every resident gets the attention they deserve.

sections.label: Clear rules, oversight, complaint system
sections.summary: It states that government intervention needs clear objective rules, public accountability, oversight and a working complaint system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If the Government needs to intervene, there must be clear, objective rules on when and how that happens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need public accountability, real oversight and a complaint system that works.

sections.label: Licensing framework for social residential homes
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a licensing framework for social residential homes, raising care standards and strengthening enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a licensing framework for social residential homes, which raises standards of care and strengthens enforcement when these standards are not met.

sections.label: Director-General approval for prescribed duties
sections.summary: Under section 19, prior approval of the Director-General is required to deploy an individual for certain prescribed duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under section 19, prior approval of the Director-General is required to deploy an individual to carry out certain prescribed duties.

sections.label: Step-in arrangements for licensees
sections.summary: Part 6 provides step-in arrangements for licensees where necessary to ensure residents' safety, welfare and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Part 6 of the Bill provides for step-in arrangements for licensees where necessary to ensure the safety, welfare and well-being of residents.

sections.label: Notifying inspecting officer of offence
sections.summary: Section 53 allows a person who suspects an offence to notify an inspecting officer of the relevant facts and circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 53 provides that a person who suspects that an offence has been committed may notify an inspecting officer of the relevant facts and circumstances.

sections.label: Minimum staffing ratios for Homes
sections.summary: MSF-funded Homes must meet MSF minimum staffing ratios, and this Bill lets MSF set such ratios for all licensed Homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Today, all Homes funded by MSF, which includes most Homes licensed under the existing Homes for the Aged Act and Children and Young Persons Act, need to abide by minimum staffing ratios set out by MSF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: This Bill will allow MSF to set out minimum staffing ratios for all licensed Homes.

sections.label: Informing Homes of assessment outcome
sections.summary: Homes are generally informed of the assessment outcome within two weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Generally, we endeavour to inform Homes of the outcome of the assessment within two weeks.

sections.label: Reports on resident abuse
sections.summary: From 2020 to 2024, MSF received an average of six reports per year on resident abuse, including excessive use of force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Over the 2020 to 2024 period, MSF received an average of six reports per year on resident abuse, including that of excessive use of force.

sections.label: Assessing facts for step-in powers
sections.summary: MSF will thoroughly assess each case's facts, such as severity of harm to residents, when deciding step-in powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In determining when and how to exercise the step-in powers, MSF will thoroughly assess the facts of each case, such as the severity of harm caused to residents.

sections.label: Home operator change in 10 years
sections.summary: Only one home changed operators in the past 10 years, after the operator decided not to continue running it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Mr Yong asked about the number of homes that have required a change of operators in the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Thus far, only one home underwent a change of operator as the operator had decided not to continue running the home following a thorough evaluation of the organisation's resources and strategic direction.

sections.label: Whistle-blower protection and referral
sections.summary: The whistle-blower will be referred to MSF inspecting officers to assist investigations and will be conferred protection under clause 53.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The whistle-blower will be referred to the MSF inspecting officers to assist investigations of the offence and will be conferred protection under clause 53.

sections.label: Penalties compared to other legislation
sections.summary: The penalties under this Bill are commensurate with comparable offences under other legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The penalties under this Bill are commensurate with that of comparable offences under other legislation.

sections.label: Transition Support Package for homes
sections.summary: MSF and NCSS have set aside a $33 million Transition Support Package for all licensable homes to invest in training, CCTV and change management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Nonetheless, MSF and NCSS have set aside a $33 million Transition Support Package for all licensable homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Mr Tan will be pleased to know that with this funding, homes will be able to invest in training for staff, updating or installing CCTV systems and change management efforts as they transit to this new licensing regime.

sections.label: Job redesign pilot with homes
sections.summary: MSF has embarked on a job redesign pilot with selected homes to attract and retain talent in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: To attract and retain talent in the sector, MSF has also embarked on a job redesign pilot with selected homes.

sections.label: Enabled Living Programme pilot
sections.summary: The Enabled Living Programme pilot is an alternative to residential care that seeks to enable persons with disabilities to live and age in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: One example is the Enabled Living Programme pilot, which is an alternative to residential care and seeks to enable persons with disabilities to live and age in the community.

sections.label: Reviewing sector's longer-term evolution
sections.summary: MSF is in the early stages of reviewing how the sector can evolve over the longer term to improve care quality, leverage technology and build capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Some seniors may have acquired disability while some persons with disabilities have aged and have become seniors themselves, so we may need to equip our homes to cater to both types of needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: We are in the early stages of reviewing how the sector can evolve over the longer term to improve care quality, leverage technology and build capabilities for better client outcomes.

sections.label: Hostel caterers and Visitors boards
sections.summary: Singapore Boys' Hostel engaged two caterers for menu variety, and MSF will expand Boards of Visitors to cover all licensable homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: To address this, the Singapore Boys' Hostel has engaged two caterers to provide greater variety in the food menu.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Under this Bill, MSF will be expanding the Boards of Visitors to cover all these licensable homes.

sections.label: Staff caring for residents
sections.summary: About 2,000 staff care for 4,000 residents, many doing shift work to supervise and assist with daily living activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Today, I want to spotlight the dedication of staff in these homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: These 4,000 residents are cared for by about 2,000 staff, many of whom are care staff doing shift work to supervise and assist residents with their activities of daily living.
